supersedes: ONIQ-VEO-LITE-VS-FAST-v1 — inputs were contaminated; see below
why_v2_exists: v1 fed Veo the raw two-pose design sheets from remotion/public/sheets/cut/. Both models rendered the sheet's caption text into the world as scenery.

The contamination was UNEQUAL: aladdin.png carries no text at all, princess.png carries a title plus four FRONT/SIDE VIEW labels. So v1's cases were not even contaminated consistently, which is a second and independent reason its absolute quality numbers cannot be used.
v1's relative Lite-vs-Fast comparison remains usable, because both models received byte-identical frames per case. v1's ABSOLUTE quality numbers do not.

input_construction.method: Front pose isolated from the ONIQ sheet by column-extent detection, placed on a plain neutral backdrop at 720x1280.
input_construction.verified: Every retained input was inspected visually at full size, not merely produced by the script.

characters_rejected.captain: residual title text and a ground-shadow plate survive the crop
characters_rejected.magician: sheet contains head portraits, not an isolated full-body pose
characters_rejected.fisherman: figure sits on a coloured panel; title text survives
characters_rejected.jarJinni: title text plus a colour-swatch strip
characters_rejected.aliBaba: sheet is three head portraits, a hand study and an axe — no clean full-body pose exists on it
characters_rejected.mother: head portrait plus a hand study

input_construction.rejection_rule: A character was retained ONLY if visual inspection confirmed: one pose, no caption, no label, no second figure, no prop study, no palette strip. Six of ten failed that and were dropped rather than cleaned up approximately.
input_construction.known_minor_residue: aladdin retains a small pale artefact near the feet; lampJinni retains its lamp and two small specks. Both were judged not to constitute text or a second figure. Recorded rather than hidden.

controls.start_frame: byte-identical file for both models, per case
controls.prompt: byte-identical string for both models, per case
controls.audio: NOT selectable on this API surface — generateAudio and six alternate spellings all return HTTP 400. Both models return an AAC track regardless. Identical for both, so it does not bias the comparison.
controls.gate: one implementation, cannot see which model produced a row
controls.retries: NONE. A failure is the measurement.

cases.prompt: The boy walks forward at a steady, even pace. Full body stays in frame. Natural arm swing.
The woman speaks directly to camera. Her lips move naturally as she talks. Small, calm head movements.
Slow push in on her face. She blinks once and her expression softens slightly.
He turns his upper body to face left, then holds the new position steadily.
Two people stand facing each other. One gestures while speaking; the other listens and nods once.
She raises one hand and slowly opens her fingers, palm toward camera.
He steps forward with one leg, the knee bending clearly, then plants his foot and settles.
The camera arcs slowly to the right around the standing figure, who remains still.
Smoke and loose cloth drift and curl in the air around the figure, who stays still.
Full-body side view. He walks with a clear, correct walking cycle; both knees bend and straighten naturally.
cases.why_this_case: The documented in-house failure mode. The ARAP CPU path over-curls the knee (batch-3 diagnostic, root cause = source BVH). It is the class in-house is known to lose, so it is the class most likely to justify paying an external provider at all.

stated_limits: Four characters across ten classes, not ten characters. Character is therefore NOT a controlled variable across classes — but it IS controlled within each case, which is what the Lite-vs-Fast comparison needs.
One generation per model per case. n=10 per model cannot separate a two-clip difference. Conclusions are PROVISIONAL, never 'model X is better'.
Prompt adherence is measured only where a defensible automatic test exists. Three classes are marked UNMEASURABLE rather than given a test that would pass on mere pixel change.
Human visual assessment will be labelled NON_BLIND unless it demonstrably was blind. The v1 review was NOT blind and must never be described as such.
